page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare metal server powered by Intel Xeon 8559C processors. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with a base clock speed of 3.6 GHz and a 320 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage is a defining feature, providing 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 95,190.03 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 22,291.0, both placing in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 6,647.5 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 119.86 GB/sec. Database operations are exceptionally strong, with Passmark database operations scoring 33,739.36 and Redis SET operations reaching 117.71 million operations per second.

This hardware configuration is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput static web serving, and data-intensive applications. While the server excels in multi-threaded tasks, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation, single-core stress-ng performance is moderate at 2,160.09. Additionally, despite the lack of dedicated GPU hardware, the Intel Xeon processor supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, enabling strong prompt processing speeds for medium and large language models, though text generation speeds remain average.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare metal server designed for data-intensive workloads. It features 96 vCPUs via an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.6 GHz, 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, and 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server delivers top-tier performance in database operations, multi-threaded decompression, and software compilation, supported by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While single-core performance is average, its multi-core capabilities are strong, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 95,190.03 and Redis SET throughput of 117.71 million operations per second. The inclusion of Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets assists with vector calculations and LLM prompt processing. This configuration is highly efficient for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and heavy data processing tasks requiring massive local storage and high memory bandwidth.
